 Advocate for : MR D MONDAL  Advocate for : appearing for NUR ISLAM AND ANR. B  BEFORE  HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ARUN DEV CHOUDHURY  ORDER 08.05.2023.
Mr. D. Mondal, learned counsel for the applicant submits that the respondent No. 1, owner cum driver of the offending vehicle is not a necessary party for determination of the present application.
Mr. Mondal, learned counsel submits that the connected appeal is filed for enhancement of compensation and there is no dispute as regards insurance policy and the driving license.

Therefore,
the respondent No. 1, presence in the present appeal is not necessary.

In that view of the matter, Mr.
Mondal, learned counsel prays that the name of the respondent No. 1 be deleted from the array of parties.

Without entering into the merit of such contention, on the prayer of Mr. Mondal, learned counsel,
the name of the respondent No. 1 is deleted from the array of parties at the risk of the applicant.
Registry to do the needful.

This is application filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 Page No.# 3/3 read with Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 for condonation of delay of 226 days in preferring the connected MAC Appeal against the Judgment and Award dated 21.06.2019 passed by the learned Member, MACT No. 3, Kamrup (M) at Guwahati in MAC Case No. 54/2018.
The cause of delay is explained at paragraphs 2 and 3 of this application.
Ms. P. Borthakur, learned counsel for the respondents submits that she will have no objection, if delay is condoned.

Considering the submissions of the learned counsel for the respondents as well as the pleadings made in the paragraphs 2 and 3 of this application, this Court is of the opinion that the present applicant was prevented by sufficient cause in preferring the connected appeal within time.
Accordingly, the delay is condoned.
IA stands disposed of.
Registry to register the connected MAC Appeal, if same is not defective and list for Admission by showing the name of Ms. P. Borthakur, learned counsel for the respondent No. 2 in the cause list.
